subject: Post-call: ACME integration & model routing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ACME integration & model routing next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + agreed next steps from our side:

1) Integration scope we discussed
   - Primary use case: customer support assistant (routing to KB + same-session retrieval)
   - Secondary: summarized transcripts and ticket triage via embeddings + reranker

2) Architecture / auth notes you asked about
   - SDK: we recommend the Redwood SDK (attached) for quick setup. It handles auth, streaming, and structured output parsing.
   - Auth options: API key for PoC; for production we recommend mTLS + workload identity or KMS-backed service accounts.

3) Model routing + policy (high-level)
   - Latency-sensitive (chat) -> low-latency model variant in us-west region
   - Cost-sensitive batch jobs (summaries/embeddings) -> cheaper quantized model with higher throughput
   - Fallbacks: primary model -> quantized variant -> smaller low-cost model for emergency overflow

Next steps (owner):
- Marissa: Send SDK + sample policy + HubSpot deal link (this email) — today
- Dev: Draft integration checklist + example routing policy + sample auth snippet — EOD tomorrow
- Acme: Share estimated monthly token volumes and any compliance requirements (PII, SOC2) — by Mon 3/23

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.md, model-routing-policy.yaml (sample), acme-ma_plan.xlsx (template)

Look forward to the next touchpoint. If useful, we can schedule a short followup with engineering to walk the sample policy.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME integration & model routing next steps

Alex — great questions. Quick answers and an implementation sketch below.

1) SOC2 / audit logs   - We can share an on-demand SOC2 report via our security portal (link sent in HubSpot). Audit logs: available in Redwood Console, exported to S3 or sent to your SIEM via webhook.

2) Reranker traces / token scores   - Yes: the embeddings + reranker pipeline can return per-candidate scores and optional token-level contribution traces. We expose a field `rerank_explain` in structured output when enabled. This is included in the SDK response object and can be toggled for cost control.

3) SDK / Auth & example code   - Attached is `redwood-sdk-setup.md`. Minimal Node example (snippet):

   const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' })

   // structured output + tool calling example
   const res = await client.chat.create({
     model: 'rwd-chat-lowlatency-v1',
     input: prompt,
     structured_output: true,
     routing_policy: 'acme_latency_priority'
   })

   // reranker call (separate call)
   const rerank = await client.rerank.create({
     embeddingModel: 'rwd-embed-1',
     candidates: candidateTexts,
     return_traces: true
   })

4) Model routing policy (sample)   - I attached `model-routing-policy.yaml` with a sample policy. High-level:
     - routes by: intent, latency requirement, region
     - policies defined: acme_latency_priority, acme_cost_saver
     - fallback chain: primary -> quantized_variant -> lowcost_fallback

5) Next steps   - If you can share token volume and retention requirements, I'll produce an estimated cost matrix for the two policies.

Happy to kick off an engineering call Tue 9:00-10:00 PT or Wed 11:00-12:00 PT. Which works?

- Dev

Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME integration & model routing next steps

Priya / Alex — quick engineering reply ahead of Tue call.

1) rerank_explain perf impact   - Enabling traces can add ~20-40ms per candidate at 8-16 candidates depending on model variant. For chat flows we usually enable sampling traces (1% or for debug) and enable full traces for reranking jobs. We can provide numbers from a benchmark run with your candidate sizes.

2) OIDC / short-lived tokens   - We support OIDC-based short-lived tokens via our Private deployment / Dedicated integrations; hosted API supports federated service accounts with OIDC exchange as well. Implementation options:
     a) Your IDP -> Redwood STS: exchange OIDC token for short-lived Redwood token (recommended)
     b) KMS + signed JWTs for on-prem customers

3) Routing policy snippet (inline example)   - policy: acme_latency_priority
     match:
       - intent: conversational
       - max_latency_ms: 75
       - region: us-west
     action:
       - route_to: rwd-chat-lowlatency-v1
       - fallback_chain: [rwd-chat-quantized-v1, rwd-chat-small-v1]

4) Action items before Tue   - Acme: share token volumes & retention/PII constraints (Priya)
   - Redwood (Dev + Marcus): generate cost-estimate table for policy `acme_latency_priority` vs `acme_cost_saver`

See you Tue 9:00 PT — calendar invite sent by Marissa.
